newsitem.title: USA: Mass. Gov. Cellucci files bill for income tax cut.
newsitem.headline: Mass. Gov. Cellucci files bill for income tax cut.

text.p: Massachusetts acting Gov. Paul Cellucci on Wednesday filed the state's largest-ever tax cut, proposing to slash the income tax to five percent from 5.95 percent currently.
"As my first official act as governor, I am sending a message to the taxpayers that I will continue to fight to give families a much-deserved break on their taxes," Cellucci said.
The measure, to be phased in over three years, would save taxpayers $1.2 billion or $600 in annual savings for the average family of two working parents, his office said.

Treasurer Joseph Malone, expected to be Cellucci's major rival for the Republican nomination for governor next year, week pledged to fight for a similiar cut in the state income tax earlier this month when he announced his run for the governor's office.
Department of Revenue estimates released Wednesday show the state has a $250 million surplus, which would serve as a down payment for the income tax cut, Cellucci's office said.
Cellucci's predecessor, former Gov. William Weld, stepped down Tuesday to fight fulltime for his nomination as ambassador to Mexico.
